findings.reason: two override records of identical shape will drift; the plan should name the existing waiver record as the mechanism to extend, or justify a parallel one, before §2 is implemented.
findings.text: §2 requires "a flag whose reason is recorded on the run and reaches the ledger row"; that is already the `--no-fence REASON` waiver (`reckon/cli.py:1815` → `fence_waiver`, recorded at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7476` as `record["fence_waiver"] = {"reason": ...}` and carried into the committed row at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7512`), and the plan neither names it nor says why the orchestrator-lane override needs a second reason-recorded flag

findings.reason: two independent walks that each answer "which configured lanes can resolve this node" will drift as the resolve/launch rules change; the plan should extend the existing walk (parameterise its predicate) rather than fork it, and name that helper in §1's discharge mechanism.
findings.text: `_orchestrator_lane_discharge_candidates` repeats the backend walk of the incumbent owner `_unmetered_dispatch_alternatives` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3532`): both iterate `sorted(config["backends"])`, call `resolve_role_override(config, role, spec_level, candidate)`, and keep candidates whose `launch` is in `("cli", "in-harness")`, differing only in the selection predicate (declares no orchestrator role vs. is unmetered)
